subQuestions.questionText:
The function of the epididymis is to …
A produce semen.
B transport sperm to the urethra.
C produce sperm.
D store sperm until maturation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
The epididymis stores sperm until they mature. Sperm production occurs in the seminiferous tubules of the testes; semen is produced by accessory glands; the vas deferens transports sperm to the urethra.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is an exocrine gland?
A Pituitary
B Prostate
C Adrenal
D Thyroid
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
The prostate is an exocrine gland because it secretes its products (prostatic fluid) through a duct. Pituitary, adrenal, and thyroid are all endocrine glands that secrete hormones directly into the blood.

subQuestions.questionText:
A list of the functions of the brain is provided below:
(i) Interprets sensation
(ii) Regulates involuntary actions
(iii) Controls higher thought processes
(iv) Controls voluntary actions
Which ONE of the following combinations are the functions of the cerebrum?
A (ii) and (iii) only
B (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
C (i), (iii) and (iv) only
D (i) and (ii) only
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
The cerebrum interprets sensation, controls higher thought processes, and controls voluntary actions. Regulating involuntary actions is the function of the medulla oblongata, not the cerebrum.

subQuestions.questionText:
An acrosome has …
A mitochondria to produce energy for the movement of sperm.
B a chromatin network that carries genes.
C enzymes needed to penetrate the ovum.
D a tail to facilitate the movement of sperm.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
The acrosome contains hydrolytic enzymes that allow the sperm to penetrate the protective layers of the ovum during fertilisation.

options.A: mitochondria to produce energy for the movement of sperm.
options.B: a chromatin network that carries genes.
options.C: enzymes needed to penetrate the ovum.
options.D: a tail to facilitate the movement of sperm.

subQuestions.questionText:
Ovulation is stimulated by an increase in the levels of …
A progesterone.
B LH.
C FSH.
D oestrogen.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
A surge in luteinising hormone (LH) triggers ovulation, causing the mature Graafian follicle to release the secondary oocyte from the ovary.

subQuestions.questionText:
Barotrauma is a common condition that occurs when pressure builds up in the middle ear. This causes the tympanic membrane to bulge. It is most common among deep-sea divers.
Divers are advised against diving when they have a middle-ear infection because the …
A auditory canal cannot equalise the pressure in the middle ear.
B Eustachian tube is blocked and air cannot enter the middle ear.
C tympanic membrane is hardened and cannot pass the vibrations onto the middle ear.
D ossicles are fused together and cannot vibrate freely in the middle ear.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
During a middle-ear infection, the Eustachian tube becomes blocked, preventing air from entering the middle ear and equalising pressure with the outside environment. This pressure imbalance causes the tympanic membrane to bulge.

options.A: auditory canal cannot equalise the pressure in the middle ear.
options.B: Eustachian tube is blocked and air cannot enter the middle ear.
options.C: tympanic membrane is hardened and cannot pass the vibrations onto the middle ear.
options.D: ossicles are fused together and cannot vibrate freely in the middle ear.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following shows the correct combination of the hormone with its target organ?
A Prolactin – Pituitary gland
B Glucagon – Pancreas
C LH – Uterus
D TSH – Thyroid gland
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) targets the thyroid gland. Prolactin targets mammary glands; glucagon targets the liver; LH targets the ovaries (or testes), not the uterus.

subQuestions.questionText:
Oogenesis takes place in the …
A uterus.
B ovary.
C cervix.
D vagina.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Oogenesis is the process of egg cell (ovum) formation, and it takes place in the ovaries.

subQuestions.questionText:
A learner conducted an investigation to determine the effect of caffeine on reaction time.
The procedure was done as follows:
• 50 male volunteers of the same age participated.
• Their reaction times were measured using a computer program.
• They were all given 200 mℓ of an energy drink that contained caffeine.
• Their reaction times were measured again every 10 minutes for 2 hours.
Which ONE of the following increased the reliability of the results obtained?
A Gender of the volunteers
B Age of the volunteers
C 50 volunteers used
D Type of caffeine used
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Reliability is increased by using a large sample size. Using 50 volunteers ensures that the results are not due to chance and that the data is repeatable. The other options relate to controlled variables (validity), not reliability.

subQuestions.questionText:
An investigation was done in which a potted plant was placed horizontally on a clinostat. The plant was exposed to uniform light from all directions. (A clinostat is a device with a disc that rotates when switched on, allowing the attached plant to rotate as well.) The stem grew vertically upwards, which indicates that the clinostat was …
A stationary and the stem showed negative geotropism.
B rotating and the stem showed positive geotropism.
C stationary and the stem showed negative phototropism.
D rotating and the stem showed positive phototropism.
(Refer to the clinostat diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
If the clinostat was stationary, gravity would act on the stem from one direction. The stem growing vertically upwards (away from gravity) demonstrates negative geotropism. Light was uniform from all directions, so phototropism is not the cause.

options.A: stationary and the stem showed negative geotropism.
options.B: rotating and the stem showed positive geotropism.
options.C: stationary and the stem showed negative phototropism.
options.D: rotating and the stem showed positive phototropism.

Both floods and droughts can damage crops and livestock, reducing food production and therefore reducing food security.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none.
Description: The part of a neuron that speeds up the transmission of an impulse.
A: Myelin sheath
B: Axon
subQuestions.memoText:
A only (2 marks)
The myelin sheath insulates the axon and enables saltatory conduction, speeding up impulse transmission. The axon itself transmits the impulse but does not on its own speed it up.

Poaching reduces species populations, and habitat destruction removes the environments species need to survive — both negatively impact biodiversity.

subQuestions.questionText:
Describe the events that lead to pregnancy from the time a zygote is formed, up to the formation of the foetus including the development of the placenta and umbilical cord.
NOTE: NO marks will be awarded for answers in the form of flow charts, tables or diagrams.
Content: (17)
Synthesis: (3)
subQuestions.memoText:
Content (max 17 marks) – Any 17 of the following points:

Development of zygote:
• The zygote divides by mitosis
• to form a (solid) ball of cells
• called the morula
• which further divides to form a hollow ball of cells
• called the blastocyst / blastula
• The blastocyst / blastula enters the uterus
• It implants in the endometrium
• This is called implantation

Formation of membranes:
• The outer layer of the embryo becomes a chorion and
• inner layer becomes an amnion
• with the amniotic fluid inside

Placenta and umbilical cord:
• After implantation the chorion develops many finger-like outgrowths
• called chorionic villi
• The endometrium together with the chorionic villi forms the placenta
• The placenta consists of blood rich embryonic and maternal tissues
• The umbilical cord develops between the foetus and the placenta
• It consists of a hollow tube
• that contains the umbilical artery
• and the umbilical vein

Foetus formation:
• Up to 8–12 weeks of development it is called the embryo
• When differentiation of tissues into organs occurs
• and now is called a foetus

[Maximum content: 17 marks]

Synthesis (3 marks) – Assessment of presentation:
Relevance (1 mark): All information provided is relevant to the question — relevant to the development from zygote to formation of placenta and umbilical cord. No irrelevant information.
Logical sequence (1 mark): Ideas arranged in a logical / cause-effect sequence — the sequence of events in the development from zygote to placenta and umbilical cord must be in logical order.
Comprehensive (1 mark): Answered all aspects required by the essay in sufficient detail — must include development from zygote to formation of placenta and umbilical cord (minimum 11 of 17 content points).

Total: Content (17) + Synthesis (3) = 20 marks
